evals.prompt: I just cloned a new TypeScript monorepo and installed ricardobizerra/skills. I want to add a new billing webhook endpoint and make sure I follow the full workflow from branching to PR. Which skills should I run and in what order?
evals.expected_output: Advises running /setup-rblf-skills first (if docs/agents/ isn't configured yet), then walks through the main engineering spine in order: (1) /git-branching to pass the Repository State Gate, sync local main, and cut a feature/ branch; (2) /feature-development (plus /database-migration or /graphql-codegen if applicable and /testing for specs); (3) /conventional-commits to stage atomic commits per layer behind validation gates; (4) /verify (which includes /code-review against origin/main); and (5) /pr when opening the pull request.
assertions: Mentions /setup-rblf-skills as the one-time onboarding precondition
Lists /git-branching before any file edits or feature work

evals.prompt: We want to set up an automated nightly GitHub Actions workflow where an agent updates our dependencies and skills, runs tests, and maintains a rolling PR without ever being able to weaken our ESLint or Playwright configs. Which skill in this repo covers designing that system?
evals.expected_output: Routes the user to /software-factory, explaining that it provides the vocabulary (Task, Trigger, Run, Runner, Orchestrator) as well as the Verification Brakes (Protected Verification Paths, Default-Branch Review Immutability, Zero-Flakiness Gates) and Rolling Ratchet task patterns.
assertions: Mentions Verification Brakes or Protected Verification Paths / Default-Branch Review Immutability

evals.prompt: I have uncommitted changes across my Prisma schema, NestJS API resolvers, Next.js pages, and generated GraphQL hooks, and I'm ready to commit and push. Which skills do I need right now?
evals.expected_output: Routes to /database-migration and /graphql-codegen if artifacts haven't been regenerated/inspected yet, then /conventional-commits to split the dirty tree into ordered staged atomic commits (backend -> backend codegen -> frontend -> frontend codegen -> docs) with pre-commit gates, followed by /verify and /git-branching (Step 8) to push and promote.
assertions: Routes to /conventional-commits to split the multi-layer changes into ordered atomic commits
Mentions /graphql-codegen or /database-migration for schema and generated artifact alignment
Mentions /verify before pushing or promoting the branch
